mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in the last three months signals a tightening labor market, which is typically associated with economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 3 months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in the last two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases > 5% in 2 months and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases > 1% in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is negative, it signals a recessionary environment with low interest rates, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to weak economic fundamentals.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 1% and GDPC1 growth < 0% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months signals strong consumer demand, which is a positive indicator for corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases over the last three months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a strong labor market, which is typically associated with economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 70% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing at a rate above 3% YoY, it signals a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis fails.
